title: Early-Exit Charges Where a Corporate Catering Service Agreement Ends Before Its Term
content:
An agreement handed back long before the last day of its term, by a client whose spend never came near the commitment, carries an early-exit charge worked out on the minimum tested against.

**Where the agreement is ended with more than twice — 2 times — the notice days printed against the catering service level still to run before the last day of its term, and the spend counted has not reached three quarters — 0.75, that is 75 per cent — of the minimum tested against**, the early-exit charge is a tenth — 0.1, that is 10 per cent — of the minimum tested against.

**Where the agreement is ended with more than the notice days printed against the catering service level but not more than twice that many still to run before the last day of its term, and the spend counted has not reached three quarters of the minimum tested against**, the early-exit charge is a twentieth — 0.05, that is 5 per cent — of the minimum tested against.

**Otherwise**, no early-exit charge is carried.

### Working the day count

Take a hypothetical Corporate Catering Service Agreement whose service level is printed with 60 notice days, whose minimum tested against is 42000.00 USD and whose spend counted stands at 20000.00 USD — short of the 31500.00 USD that three quarters of the minimum comes to.

| Days still to run before the last day of the term | Early-exit charge |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | 4200.00 USD, a tenth of 42000.00 USD |
| 121 | 4200.00 USD |
| 120 | 2100.00 USD, a twentieth of 42000.00 USD |
| 61 | 2100.00 USD |
| 60 | none |
| 20 | none |

Exactly twice the notice days still to run is not *more* than twice that many, so 120 days falls on the second branch; exactly the notice days still to run is not more than the notice days, so 60 days carries no charge. Where the same agreement's spend counted had instead reached 31500.00 USD or more, no early-exit charge would be carried at any of those day counts.
